name: Risograph Two-Drum Print
summary: Two riso inks on uncoated paper: the first drum prints your dashboards, and Acme Pulse is the coral second drum that lands only where something is wrong.
look: Warm uncoated stock with speckle grain, coarse halftone dots and crop marks. Teal and fluorescent coral print as semi-transparent layers in multiply, a few pixels off-register, so every overlap turns deep green-black and the whole film steps along at 12 fps like a flip-book.

components.name: Paper + grain
components.role: uncoated stock with an SVG feTurbulence speckle multiplied over everything

components.name: Halftone field
components.role: SVG dot patterns (teal 45°, coral 15°) where dot size carries the value

components.name: Misregistered headline
components.role: two stacked copies (teal, coral) in multiply, 3–8 px apart

components.name: Crop marks + colour bar
components.role: printer furniture that signals a physical proof

components.name: Flag stamp
components.role: circular coral stamp with ring text; the agent's signature on the anomaly

components.name: Overprint button
components.role: coral block with an off-register teal outline; the human action

motion.name: Plate-by-plate build
motion.how: teal drum prints, coral lands 4 frames later; everything stepped at 12 fps so each plate hit sits on an 8th note at 120 BPM

motion.name: Registration wobble
motion.how: the coral layer drifts 1–2 px per frame from a seeded offset table

motion.name: Dot-grow reveal
motion.how: halftone radius 0→full, power2.out over 0.5 s (one beat), like ink soaking into paper

story: Hook: twelve halftone dashboard tiles stamp in and 'And the drop still shipped on Friday.' prints teal, then coral. Reveal: on the drop a coral halftone disc dot-grows behind the Acme mark and a giant two-plate 'Acme Pulse'. Proof: a teal sheet of healthy metrics prints; the coral pass hits only the 'Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231' row with a FLAGGED stamp, and a coral Roll back button waits for the human. CTA: 'Caught before customers noticed.' in two plates, lockup and an off-register Start free block.
adapt: Print your own table or dashboard as plate 1 and let plate 2 hit only the rows your product flags; the stamp text becomes your status label.
